question: What current-generation workload economics can now be proved from public evidence?
conclusion: A narrow successful-work comparison is now reproducible from raw public records: on a pinned Rust build, same-shape Xeon 6 and AMD Turin AWS instances both pass the same tests, while the AMD runs finish sooner and cost less under an explicitly normalized EC2-plus-EBS estimate. The stronger claim of a complete actual cloud bill or enterprise TCO remains unproved. Nothing here identifies Intel's net chip price or retained profit.

status.successful_work_observed: verified from all 10 original primary-pair GitHub job logs
status.raw_arithmetic_independently_reproducibl: yes, offline from archived records and calculate_matched_build.py
status.complete_actual_cloud_bill: not identified; source fields are cost estimates, not AWS CUR/invoices
status.exact_physical_resources_equal: no: advertised vCPU/RAM/storage match, physical core mapping differs

new_primary_source.commercial_interest: RunsOn is a CI-runner software vendor comparing its offering with other runner providers. It operates this test. No CPU-vendor sponsorship is identified in the inspected sources, but that is not independent verification of funding or an external audit.
new_primary_source.quality: Every primary-pair original job log reports the same 45 named tests passing, with no failures or skips. The ten logs also contain the same observed set of 470 compiled crate/version pairs and the pinned source/toolchain. All recorded formatting, test and both Clippy phases succeed.
new_primary_source.pinned_workload: aome510/spotify-player@7dc9d17a7bf5671eb6129fdf9127729f659637fc with Rust 1.98.1, same features, no build cache
new_primary_source.workflow_audit: The rust.yml file at each of the five actual harness commits has the same SHA256, 14a119fcac905fa85180b475c3fb216aca7956181c323944d2c0edd3a1852128.
new_primary_source.matching: Each Intel/AMD pair shares 8 advertised vCPU, 32 GiB advertised RAM, 30 GB root EBS, OS, kernel, AMI and harness commit. Within-pair x64 binaries/toolchain path match by configuration, though binary-output hashes were not published. Different runs include a kernel/image update; each pair still matches.
new_primary_source.CPU_mapping: m8i.2xlarge exposes 4 Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores with 2 threads/core. m8a.2xlarge exposes 8 EPYC 9R45 cores with 1 thread/core. This compares purchasable AWS products, not equal-core CPU architecture.
new_primary_source.geography: All us-east-1; two pairs use the same AZ, three different us-east-1 AZs. On-demand list rates are regional. Network/download timing and placement effects are not randomized.
new_primary_source.lifecycle: All five Intel primary runs used spot; AMD used spot four times and on-demand once. The main economic comparison reprices all recorded instance windows at current on-demand rates. No claim that all ten were observed on-demand runs.

headline.success_interpretation: These are five repeated paired batches, not 450 independent measurements or evidence of a production reliability percentile. Tests establish this project's accepted correctness checks, not every possible application requirement.
headline.latency_interpretation: No ex-ante production SLA is claimed. The entire observed AMD job-time range is below the entire observed Intel range. Queue-plus-job ranges are also separated (AMD 100–112 seconds, Intel 123–138). Five samples cannot establish p99 or fleet capacity.

billing_audit.primary_formula: sum[billedSeconds/3600 * (current AWS on-demand EC2 rate + raw EBS hourly estimate)] / successful jobs
billing_audit.recorded_cost_meaning: bin/runs-on-costs.py explicitly reads estimated_cost_usd and estimated_ec2_cost_usd from the operator's control plane. Calling these actual paid invoices would be wrong.
billing_audit.EBS: Source uses $0.018356/hour, consistent with 30 GB gp3 at 400 MiB/s: (30*$0.08 + (400-125)*$0.04)/730 hours. Main calculation preserves that source estimate; a sensitivity uses actual calendar month hours.
billing_audit.missing_IPv4: The public benchmark collector sums EC2 and EBS only. The provider's separate real-repository blog methodology explicitly includes public IPv4, but says it is not the fixed benchmark methodology. We therefore add one $0.005/hour public IPv4 only as an explicit scenario, not an observed address-charge fact.
billing_audit.source_time_conflict: The archived raw control-plane estimated windows average 126.76 seconds Intel and 98.46 seconds AMD. Original job logs also show a separate estimate with 20 seconds for shutdown; those windows are longer. Their exact reconciliation to resource termination and invoice time is unavailable.

cost_scenarios.name: Raw control-plane window, current on-demand EC2, calendar-month EBS, one assumed IPv4
Alternate original job-log window including stated shutdown allowance, current on-demand EC2, calendar-month EBS, one assumed IPv4

omitted_fields: AWS CUR or invoice line items tied to instance and volume resource IDs, including exact start/termination/allocation/release times and billing rounding.
Actual public-IP allocation count/lifetime or confirmed private/NAT networking design, instead of assuming one public IPv4.
Network bytes and charged destinations, artifact/storage/request costs, monitoring/logging/bootstrap/control-plane costs.
A defined buyer deployment volume and allocation of license/controller fixed costs; both can cancel in a defined marginal choice but are not zero total costs.
Any savings plans/reservations, volume discounts, credits, taxes, paid support, operational/migration cost and production SLA/failure-retry behavior.
billing_audit.hurdle_interpretation: An additional unmeasured AMD-specific cost of about $0.001735 per job would erase the primary direct-cost advantage. Equal fixed fees do not change the absolute gap but do reduce its percentage of total cost. Do not claim omissions cannot reverse ranking without measuring their differential.
billing_audit.cloud_price_break_even: At these observed windows, Intel EC2 compute would need about $0.374083/hour rather than $0.42336/hour to match AMD's primary direct cost (11.64% lower). This is AWS retail pricing arithmetic, not an Intel CPU discount or required change in Intel's ASP.

robustness.two_and_four_vCPU: All five same-size Intel/AMD runs also succeed at 2 and 4 vCPU. Their reconstructed on-demand EC2+EBS cost reductions are approximately 30.99% and 20.75% respectively. These sizes use different physical-core mappings and may use zram; retain as diagnostics, not more independent primary experiments.
robustness.Arm: Graviton5 m9g.2xlarge also has five successful source records with 8vCPU/32GiB and an estimated normalized direct cost of $0.011522 per build. It compiles for a different architecture and its full logs were not the primary verification target, so it is secondary rather than part of the main claim.
robustness.no_population_stats: No significance level or confidence interval is claimed. Job order, host placement, CPU contention, package downloads and all broader production conditions are not experimentally controlled.
robustness.sample_selection: Primary source chosen after seeing headline rankings; selection policy recorded before the raw reanalysis. The five most recent complete scheduled Rust runs were retained, not the best five runs for a vendor.

comparison_with_existing_candidates.why_not_full_match: Old Intel versus new Intel, not AMD; absolute successful token output, quality and latency insufficient; CPU-only headline excludes required memory. Already audited in prior research.
Open raw configurations and same task hashes, but mixed dates, incomplete client/error retention, no production latency threshold; aggregate output cannot repair success denominator. Already audited.
Intel commissioned; shared truncated recordings yield Failed strict replay status, so cost per scheduled trial differs from cost per successful task. Already audited.
Audited hardware/software/maintenance quotes and accepted SQL results, but memory, storage, OS, date and topology differ. TPC quote excludes complete enterprise TCO. Already audited.
Primary independent published charts accessible; raw OpenBenchmarking endpoint again returned403. Charts alone do not supply full success/error/billing records.
Inspection found report plus scripts but no committed raw trial records in results directory, and report labels the Intel m8i family Emerald Rapids. Not used for a numerical conclusion.

comparison_with_existing_candidates.why_selected: Best newly found public combination of pinned executable recipe, multiple paired current-generation runs, direct correctness-test logs and per-job cost-window estimates. Still lacks a complete invoice and an independently repeated experiment.

investment_use.valid: A named third-party runner operator successfully executes an identical x64 build on present Xeon6 and Turin cloud offerings. The cheapest advertised hourly instance need not minimize successful-work cost. This gives concrete current competitor pressure and narrows the buyer-value evidence gap.
invalid: This proves AMD has lower complete TCO for every customer, or Intel has no valuable workload niche.
This proves Intel CPU architecture is 23.7% slower per core; physical-core counts differ.
This proves AWS passes a specific CPU procurement discount to buyers, or reveals Intel net ASP/manufacturing cost.
This justifies subtracting the workload saving directly from Intel DCAI margin or changing company revenue/share forecasts.
This is our original cloud experiment, an independent hardware audit, or a fully reconciled customer invoice.
investment_use.proof_matrix_update: Split the broad open claim into (1) successful matched x64 workflow and bounded direct-cost estimate, now supported, and (2) complete actual buyer cost plus Intel value capture, still unproved. Do not upgrade the original full-cost winner claim to already_verified.

reproduction.no_network_needed: The calculation reads the frozen local raw source archive only.
reproduction.original_work: Parsed 45 job records, checked 10 primary original logs, independently re-priced their windows from official AWS data, checked all five exact workflow versions, and computed cost/success and omission sensitivities.
